long_biography.plain_text:
Dan Stabbert grew up aboard his father Fred's converted medical missionary vessel, learning machinery and seamanship from childhood and obtaining a captain's licence at seventeen. That family environment supplied uncommon maritime training. Dan and Cheryl Stabbert nevertheless founded their own company in 1978, beginning with one tug and expanding through vessel purchases, conversions and operating contracts.

As president and chief executive of Stabbert Maritime, Stabbert built an integrated group spanning offshore and research-vessel operations, ship repair, technical project management and major vessel conversions. He combined the roles of owner, captain and chief engineer, repeatedly buying overlooked craft and returning them to commercial service. The business later added shipyard capacity in Seattle and Anacortes while its fleet supported scientific, subsea-energy and maritime-service work worldwide.
